title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A release no longer depends on how busy the laptop is
summary: Thirteen tests asserted a wall clock budget, some as low as 50 milliseconds. The publish script runs the suite, so a busy machine stopped a release that had nothing wrong with it.

highlights.title: Judged by the fastest run, not the first
highlights.description: A first call carries the warm up of everything it touches: 28 milliseconds cold against 7 warm on a calm machine, 108 against 17 on a busy one.

sections.heading: Internal
bullets: The timing budgets in the test suite are judged by the fastest of up to three runs, and the retry only happens when the first run misses, so a calm machine pays nothing. Measured over interleaved pairs, the suite takes the same time it did.
One publish had already stopped on 422 milliseconds against a 300 millisecond budget while the steady state cost of that workload is 5 milliseconds.
